## 1. Current launch verdict

# NOT READY

Rekoda is code-complete against its build plan and its test estate is
unusually strong. It runs on staging (deployed after CI on `main`), where
the Meta WhatsApp transport has been live-exercised (real webhook ingress,
outbound text and media); nothing has run in production. The deployment
runtime is code complete (G-01: images, production compose, Caddy, the
migrate job, proved on a clean CI runner) but no production host is
provisioned, and there is no backup mechanism, no production WhatsApp
number (Meta App Review and templates remain open), no production Paystack
path (payment-provider live verification remains pending), no company facts on the legal pages, and the AI
has never been measured against a real model. G-06 (refund, reversal and chargeback webhooks absorbed) is CODE COMPLETE as of 11 September 2026 against provider fixtures and Paystack's published samples, and NOT LIVE PROVIDER VERIFIED: the live envelopes are still to be confirmed under G-05. Two financial defects stand between the books and real money: G-11 (VAT hardcoded to
zero on three sale paths; OD-2 may record a deferral for a beta with no
VAT-registered merchant) and G-22 (merchant processing fee estimated from the
wrong rate card); Chat purchase duplicate protection is code complete and in review (G-81), with
recorded residuals (G-92(5) books one real purchase twice under OD-23 D3 as ruled), while G-89 (a
dashboard PO receive is not compared with Chat bookings) and G-87 (a resend the model reads as an
expense) stay open and are required before public launch; G-61 (a transfer-paid purchase credited Cash on Hand) is merged, staging acceptance in progress. The verdict moves to **READY FOR
STAGING** when the P0 items in §4 that are code gaps are closed and a
staging environment boots end to end; to **READY FOR PRIVATE BETA** when the §14
private-beta bar is met (P0 code gaps closed; G-03, G-04 and G-05 carried on
a test WABA, staging legal placeholders and test-mode Paystack keys; every P1
closed or deferred by a ruling in §6) and journeys J1 to J13, J17, J19 and J20
pass on staging with real providers in test mode; to **READY FOR PUBLIC LAUNCH** when the owner-held
external dependencies in §5 close and GATE 12 passes.

## 2. Launch target

- **Product:** Rekoda Chat first (merchant talks to Rekoda on WhatsApp plus the shared dashboard). Integrate's storefront and WhatsApp-catalogue orders are built; merchant-owned WABA connection has no HTTP surface and Meta app review is open, so Integrate ships to a private cohort only after W0 closes.
- **Market:** Nigeria, NGN only (ADR 0033).
- **Providers at launch:** Meta Cloud API (WhatsApp), Anthropic (reasoning, vision), OpenAI (transcription, optional verifier), Paystack (collection, merchant-owned accounts, Pay-with-Transfer), Cloudflare R2 (documents), Hetzner + Cloudflare (hosting per ADR 0006). Mono, OPay and Kuda stay production-disabled.
- **Shape of the first cohort:** a private beta of hand-held merchants on test-mode Paystack keys, then live keys after the §47 written confirmation.

## 3. Current verified state (summary)

See `REKODA_CURRENT_STATE.md` §3 for the capability table. In one paragraph: identity, tenancy, RLS, webhook verification, the chat gates, the ledger kernel, statements, exports, the storefront, the public API and metering are verified complete in CI; the Meta WhatsApp transport has been live-exercised on staging (real webhook ingress, outbound text and media), while production Meta App Review and templates are still pending; payment-provider live verification is pending; voice, vision, AI interpretation, R2 storage, retention, the queue and billing are implemented and remain unverified against their live providers; suppliers, tax calculation, notifications, sweeps scheduling, observability, legal pages and the admin surface are partial; the deployment runtime is code complete and proved on a clean CI runner; staging runs `main` and no production host is provisioned yet (G-01); backups do not exist as code.

| G-24 | Consent              | **CODE COMPLETE (1 Oct 2026, merged in #259 (`f5ef123`)); staging acceptance pending.** Now ONE consent matcher (`consentKeyword` in `packages/core/src/router.ts`) serves `routeMessage`, `customerConsentIntent` and `consentIntentOf` (typed text, tapped reply id and title). It reads the RAW message as GRAPHEMES (what a person sees as one character, via `Intl.Segmenter`), never the forgiving normaliser, and judges each grapheme on its raw form, never on an NFKC expansion. In order: a bidi override or isolate (U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069), which reorders what is shown, refuses; the invisible format characters (zero-width space, direction marks, word joiner, soft hyphen) are removed, then surrounding SPACES and at most ONE trailing line break (CRLF counts as one), and nothing else; what remains, if longer than 512 code units, is refused before segmenting; the message must be ONE line (any LF, CR, vertical tab, form feed, NEL, U+2028 or U+2029 left after that refuses, so for a START a LEADING line break refuses: `\nSTART`, `\vSTART!`, `\r\nstart` and ` \nstart` re-subscribe nobody (Codex review), and `start\n\n` refuses too). A STOP-class word is read GENEROUSLY here too (final-head review): EMPTY lines before or after it are not content, so `\nSTOP`, `\r\nstop` and `STOP\n\n` opt out (a missed STOP keeps messaging somebody, and the model cannot opt anyone out, G-80); a STOP with real content on another line (`stop\nI will pay`) is still refused. The keyword is the run of letter graphemes (letters read through NFKC, so full-width and mathematical letters count; spaces inside allowed for `stop all`), matched against two `Set`s (STOP: `stop`, `stop all`, `stopall`, `unsubscribe`, `quit`; START: `start`, `unstop`, `subscribe`), so a message reading `constructor` matches nothing. Everything before and after it must be DECORATION: whitespace, one punctuation or symbol code point, or one emoji grapheme (a keycap such as `1️⃣`, a flag, a skin-toned emoji and a whole ZWJ family each count as ONE). Nothing that reads as a letter or a digit is decoration: an enclosed or parenthesised letter (`ⓑ`, `🅑`, `⒝`, `①`), a lone regional indicator, `ℹ`, or any symbol whose NFKC form holds a letter or digit, so `stop ⓑⓨ ⓜⓨ ⓢⓗⓞⓟ` and `stop 🇧 🇾 🇲 🇾` opt nobody out. Carve-outs, kept as decoration on purpose: `№`, `℃`, `™`, `®`, `©`, and keycaps (so `stop 5️⃣0️⃣0️⃣0️⃣` opts out, the cheap direction). It is ASYMMETRIC because the two mistakes do not cost the same. A STOP-class word may carry up to 16 decoration graphemes on each side (the longest genuine form seen is ten exclamation marks): before it, anything but a dash, plus at most one list bullet (`-` or `•` then a space), so `-----stop-----` is refused; after it, anything, including any emoji (refusals too). So `STOP!!!!!!`, `STOP,`, `"STOP"`, `*STOP*`, `🛑STOP🛑`, `(stop)`, `- stop`, `STOP :)`, `stop —`, `stop。`, `STOP/`, `STOP#`, `STOP%`, `STOP 1️⃣`, `STOP №`, `> stop`, `{stop}` and `...quit...` all stop, and so do `stop?`, `quit?` and `unsubscribe?`: a question-shaped STOP is treated as a STOP. That is a deliberate asymmetry (a START would reverse it), and the owner ruled it (OD-22, OWN-20). A START-class word keeps the strict shape, because a false START re-subscribes somebody: nothing before the word, then at most five of `.`, `!` (including `…`, full-width forms, `❗` and `❕`), an AFFIRMING emoji from a closed list (👍 👌 💯 ✅ ✔ ☑ 🙏 🙂 😊 ☺ 😀 😃 😄 🎉 ❤, any skin tone or style), or a country flag that does not spell a refusal (`🇳🇴` reads NO and is refused). So `START 👍`, `start ✅🙏🏾` and `START 🇳🇬` re-subscribe; `start 🛑`, `start ❌`, `start 🚫`, `start ⛔`, `start 👎`, `start 🙅`, `start 😡`, `start 🤔`, `start 🤷`, `start 😕`, `start 🇳🇴`, any ZWJ family, a keycap, and any question mark (`?`, `❓`, `❔`, `⁉`, `‼`, `〰`, `〽`) do not. A padded keyword (`-----start-----`, 400 dashes around `start`, `*start*`, `"start"`), `stop` followed by 400 dashes or 2,000 `!`, a sentence (`stop by my shop`, `start the generator`, `stop.` followed by another line), Cyrillic look-alikes or politeness (`please stop`, `oya stop`) changes nobody's consent; it goes to the model like any other sentence. A STOP-class word repeated up to FIVE times (`REPEATED_STOP_MAX`), the same word each time and separated only by decoration or run together ("STOP STOP", "stop!!! stop!!!", "stopstop"), is a STOP; six or more is refused; mixed words ("stop start", "STOP quit") and any repeated START are refused. The 512-unit length gate counts the message after removing invisible characters, surrounding spaces and one trailing line break, so trailing spaces never refuse a STOP. Known and accepted: a pair of regional indicators that is not a real country (an invalid "flag") counts as a flag after START, which only the sender can do to themselves. Genuine forms still REFUSED: `1. stop`, `-stop`, `--stop`, `stop-all`, `stop_all`, a STOP with more than 16 decoration graphemes on a side (base heard "stop" followed by 17 `!`), and `start :)`, `start ;)`, `START. 👍`, `start . 👍`. For a STOP these are MISSED opt-outs, not a safe direction: they are accepted as the trade-off against pasted text mutating consent, and the cap value is an OPEN OWNER DECISION (OD-20). A refused START is the safe direction. NOT YET deterministic: Pidgin and polite opt-outs (`abeg stop`, `please stop`, `stop o`, `stop na`) still go to the model, which has no consent intent (G-80). Voice and photo text reach the same matcher: a voice note transcribed as "Stop." opts out, exactly as on base; OCR text doing the same is G-78. RUNTIME NOTE: grapheme boundaries and Unicode properties come from the runtime's ICU (CI runs Node 24; local runs Node 22, ICU 77.1); only code points unassigned in one version can be classified differently, and an unassigned code point is never an affirming emoji or a START mark, so a version difference can only add STOP decoration, never a wrong START. Was: the keyword lookup ran on the normalised message before the paste guard, so a punctuation-padded `start` re-subscribed an opted-out merchant (padded `stop`, `unsubscribe` and `quit` the same way), and the customer path had no guard at all | G-49 | Payments             | **CLOSED: staging accepted (reported by the owner) after #256 merged as `2abb8a1`.** Merged as #253 (`ea7c7db`, 26 Sep 2026). On 28 Sep 2026 staging found the dashboard confirmation screen resetting the amount to the balance (React reset the uncontrolled form after the server action), so "Yes, record it" booked the balance and lost the excess; #256 made the form's amount and method controlled, bound the confirmation to the method on the server too, and added browser coverage (`apps/web/e2e/overpayment.spec.ts`); the two-step was then physically re-tested. Owner ruling OWN-16. Now a merchant overpayment is real money: an overpaid sale (chat or public API) and a later chat or dashboard payment the merchant confirmed as an overpayment record the full amount received, allocate only up to the balance, post DR Cash or Bank (the full amount) / CR Accounts Receivable or revenue (the balance) / CR Customer credits (the excess, never revenue), write an `overpaid` EXCEPTION reconciliation row for every overpayment (so the refund, reversal and chargeback guards refuse it, as for a provider overpayment), and grant `customer_credits` keyed on the payment when the invoice names a customer; with no customer the liability is booked unlinked and no customer is invented. The receipt names the excess as customer credit or as an unapplied amount not linked to a customer (`excessDisposition`). A later payment is booked over the balance only with an explicit confirmation of the balance the merchant was shown (chat: the draft's `confirmation_context`, migration 0152; dashboard: a two-step `confirm_overpayment` answer that writes nothing), and a balance that moved in between writes nothing and asks again. The public API's `POST /api/v1/payments` still refuses. Was: a merchant-reported (chat or dashboard) payment larger than the invoice balance is refused with a CG1 question and `recordMerchantPayment` throws `BalanceMoved`; there is no path for the excess to become customer credit, which spec §14.1 and journey C11 require for an overpayment. The same holds for money taken with a sale (26 Sep 2026, found during G-48): an overpaid `RecordSale` (`paidK > totalK`, from chat or the public API) records the payment at the full stated amount but allocates and posts only the total, grants no credit and records the excess nowhere, while the chat preview (`packages/core/src/gates.ts`) tells the merchant "I will note it as a credit"; since G-48 its merchant-recorded receipt states the excess was not applied to the invoice, without promising a credit. Provider-verified overpayments already create the credit Now every deterministic intent is classified in `@rekoda/core` `DETERMINISTIC_ACCESS` (exhaustive over the intent union) and checked after routing, before its handler runs: STOP, START, the erasure ceremony (the merchant's data-protection right; spec §4.5), the dashboard link, `help`, greetings, a bare number and `upgrade` work on every plan; on a live plan `who owes me`, `records`, `stock`, `payment details` and `remind` need `REKODA_CHAT`, exactly as the free-form request does; `resend` needs it on every plan. A lapsed plan is the one deliberate exception to free-form parity (OD-18): it keeps those five fixed reads (`who owes me`, `records` and `payment details` because `trialEnded` promises them; `stock` on metering-v1 §3, reading is never gated; `remind` on spec §4.5, existing invoices stay collectible) while the same request in free form gets `trialEnded`. Yes, no and cancel are never refused by their words; a "yes" is judged by the draft it would confirm (an erasure ask excepted) before anything is metered, claimed or retired, and its reply opens "I did not save that." A lapsed paid plan is told its plan ended, never that a free trial did, on every Chat surface (model path, voice and photo included). On a plan without Chat, `help` (naming only what the member's role can run), greetings, START, a stray number, an empty yes and a failed dashboard link name only what works. A Build 6 resumed read follows `records`. A refusal calls no model, meters nothing, sends nothing but its reply and writes nothing. English and Pidgin phrasings share one intent. Development and test keep their fakes. | G-74 | Config               | CLOSED in code (13 Sep 2026). Was: `REKODA_EDGE_PROXIES` is the one client-address trust list no Rekoda process reads. Now a one-shot `edge-check` job in the app image reads the same value compose gives Caddy and refuses a universal or effectively universal list by exactly the G-72 rule (0.0.0.0/0, ::/0, the mapped ::ffff:0:0/96, an IPv6 range holding the mapped block, anything reaching public space wider than an IPv4 /8 or IPv6 /16), plus the spellings Caddy could not read anyway (a comma-separated list, a shorthand address, an unknown keyword). Caddy waits for that job, so a bad value fails the deployment instead of serving. Cloudflare's published ranges, a single address and the documented empty value pass; `private_ranges`, and any range holding the edge network's gateway, are refused since G-75 | G-81 | Purchases            | **CODE COMPLETE (2 Oct 2026, in review on `fix/purchase-cross-actor-idempotency`); staging acceptance pending.** An owner-prioritised interstitial accounting-integrity fix (OD-23, OWN-21). Was: a "yes" confirms the newest pending draft business-wide and nothing compared a new purchase with one waiting or booked, so two previews of one real purchase (two members, or one member double-sending) or a purchase sent again after it was booked could be booked twice: two expenses, two postings, two stock deliveries, two bills. Now: a purchase about to be previewed is compared with every purchase of the same total waiting or booked in the last 24 hours (`purchaseMatches`, `packages/core/src/purchase-identity.ts`); only a different stated supplier reference, or two different catalogue-linked products, on BOTH sides proves it separate (supplier rows never do, D3 refinement); the question asked at the preview names every match except the member's own single waiting preview (left for D4(2), G-92(7)) and "separate" excuses exactly those (`asked_about_drafts`, `asked_about_expenses`); a question asked when a yes is refused names the first booking the purchase work found, and any other is asked about after "separate"; records are read by message order; the member's own waiting preview is replaced (Build 7's rule); anything else is HELD (migration 0158) and asked "Is this the same purchase?" through a typed, member-scoped, expiring continuation; "same" writes nothing, "separate" shows a FRESH preview with its own G-23 window; a yes to the question re-asks it and never claims an older preview; the final net is in `recordPurchaseWork` (advisory lock by business and total, re-read of bookings, refusal before the first posting, run inside a savepoint at the yes). Supersedes the G-68 note that two members may each send the same purchase and get two previews, and the matching note in `REKODA_CURRENT_STATE.md` §5.7. Scope (owner direction, 2 Oct 2026): G-81 closes Chat purchase collision handling and protects Chat against booked purchase facts, including bookings from a received purchase order (PO first, then Chat: detected and asked when the PO receive committed before the chat yes). G-89 remains OPEN as the dashboard PO-receive side (Chat first, then a matching PO receive: booked again without asking), so the system-wide one-purchase-one-truth invariant is NOT certified until G-89 closes. The work-layer lock (`LOCK_CLASS.purchaseIdentity`) is a backstop: Chat yeses are already serialised by the business lock, and PO receive does not take it (G-89). A supplier reference is stored only as a document KIND from a closed set (invoice, receipt, waybill, PO, other) and its digits, never letters (`INV:2231`; "TOLU-77" stores no letters; ADR 0005), and the bill shows "Invoice 2231"; only two references of the same named kind prove a purchase separate (an invoice number never proves anything against a receipt number, and kind other never proves); a marked amount, the purchase's own total, a separated date, a compact date of six to eight digits, a year, a year and month either way round ("INV 202610", "INV 102026") or a time with a colon after a marker ("receipt 120000" equal to the total, "NGN150K", "INV-2026-10-02", "INV-20261002", "INV 031026", "INV 2026", "INV 10:30") is never a reference; nor is anything with two runs of digits, two document words, or letters touching the number that are not a reference word ("INV I231", a possible misread of "1231"). Other amount-, date-, time- and phone-like shapes can still be kept (unmarked amounts other than the total, "INV 31026", "INV 3126", "INV 1030", "INV 08031234"), and two different numbers of the same kind always prove separate, including a misread or mistyped one (D3 as ruled); both are recorded as G-92. Trusted-product proof is DORMANT: nothing writes `external_catalogue_id` today, so no live purchase is proven separate by product; before any catalogue writer ships, product proof must never resolve products by raw name match. Known and recorded, not fixed: a resend the model labels `RecordExpense` is not compared (G-87, recorded by #261 and linked to G-81: it STAYS OPEN as this fix's follow-up, not closed here); extraction variance in the total hides a duplicate (the total is the anchor by design); the posting itself has no ledger-level backstop (G-88). Integrated with G-65 (#261, merged as `29dc934`): "same" writes nothing and is allowed on every plan, with copy that invites no refused yes; "separate" meets `fundingGateRefusal` (Chat draft access) before anything is drafted; the re-ask and the closed reply are gated with `draftRefusalWithoutChat`, as #261 gates `reaskRetiredQuestion` and `closedQuestionReply`. | G-89 | Purchases            | **OPEN, REQUIRED PRE-PUBLIC-LAUNCH (owner directed 2 Oct 2026; accounting integrity; NOT an accepted residual).** G-89: cross-ingress purchase duplicate protection for dashboard PO receive. Current behaviour: PO receive is idempotent for PO identity (the open to received claim plus `po-receive:<po.id>`); it does not check Chat-booked purchases. PO first, then Chat: G-81 detects it when the PO receive committed before the chat yes; a receive still in flight is not seen, since PO receive takes no lock (G-89). Chat first, then PO: the dashboard books it again without asking. Required behaviour: a PO receive is compared under the same OD-23 / OWN-21 policy, not a second policy. No possible duplicate: receive normally. Exact trusted identity: no second booking. Possible duplicate: an explicit possible-duplicate state to the dashboard asking SAME PURCHASE or SEPARATE PURCHASE; never receive silently, never reject permanently. SAME: no second purchase, stock, cash, bank or AP posting, bill or other financial truth, and the UI says what happened to the PO (stays open, linked, or an explicit terminal status, designed in G-89). SEPARATE: receive normally; a merchant must never be forced to abandon a genuine second purchase. Until it closes, the system-wide one-purchase-one-truth invariant is not certified (G-81 covers Chat only). (4) WITHDRAWN (final-head review of 5bfe87e): a held draft past its window is ignored by every read (`wasAskedAbout` and `askedHeldNewerThan` require a live window, and the yes skips held drafts), so it never blocks a yes; tested by "11. an expired question cannot execute". (5) Two DIFFERENT numbers of the same kind always prove separate, as OD-23 D3 rules, so a misread or mistyped digit ("invoice 2231" typed, "INV 2281" read off a photo of the same invoice), or a number the model labels with the wrong kind, books one purchase twice with no question; it needs no model error at all when two different documents of one kind belong to one purchase, for example the supplier's "receipt 0093" from one member and a POS or transfer slip's "Receipt No 4471" from another (numbers of ten digits or more are already refused); this is the literal ruling, recorded so the owner can revisit it (for example, asking when two same-kind numbers differ by one digit). (6) The preview compares the reference parsed from the model's raw command, while the yes compares the stored form, so some shapes (an eight-digit date behind a letter prefix, "INV-EMK-20261002") are kept at the preview and dropped at the yes: the preview is shown with no question and the yes is then refused and asked; nothing is booked twice. (7) The same-member rebuild rule (`rebuiltPurchaseFate`, called from `afterNewPreview`) decides by total and references only: it ignores a "separate" answer's declared records (`separate_from`) and two different trusted products (dormant until a catalogue writer exists). So in a rare sequence (a member's funding-answer rebuild and another own preview both pending, a resend asked about both, then "separate") the fresh preview supersedes the rebuild the member just declared a different purchase; the reply says it was replaced, and nothing is booked twice. A sibling: whenever a held question does not name the asking member's own waiting preview of the same total (the question is about another member's preview or about any booking, so the own preview was left for D4(2) and not named), that preview is replaced when they answer "separate", with no warning in the question; the reply says so and nothing is booked twice. (9) If a refused yes comes from a sender with no member id, the draft is held but no question continuation opens, so nobody can answer it and it lapses after 600 seconds; only members can say yes (`mayTransact`), so this is unreachable today, and nothing is booked or lost (the purchase can be sent again). (10) A "same" answer closes older retired funding questions and its held question, but if the "same" reply is never delivered neither is put back (unlike a new preview's reply, which records what it closed), so a later "cash" gets the closed-question reply; nothing is booked or lost, and the purchase can be sent again. (8) `newPurchaseFacts` falls back to the application clock when the message's arrival cannot be read, mixing clocks; the chat path always has an arrival, and the yes-time backstop does not use it ## 10. End-to-end test journeys

J1–J3 state preconditions, test data, action, expected WhatsApp reply,
expected API and database state, expected accounting entries, expected PDF
or dashboard result, expected audit record and the pass condition; the
later journeys state the subset that applies to them, always ending in a
pass condition. "Local" journeys run today against the stub sender and a local
Postgres through the existing integration harness (`apps/api/src/channels/meta.integration.test.ts`
already covers most of their steps); "staging" journeys need the named
provider. Do not execute provider-dependent journeys until staging exists
and the keys are test-mode.

### J1 · New merchant onboarding

- **Preconditions:** empty database; web and API in production mode with legal facts set; `META_OTP_TEMPLATE` approved (staging).
- **Test data:** phone `+2348030000001` (or a real test handset on staging); business "Ada's Provisions", type retail.
- **Action:** `/start` with the phone; enter the code; `/setup/business`; complete.
- **Expected WhatsApp:** one AUTHENTICATION template carrying the code, delivered within 30 s; no free-form text.
- **Expected API/DB:** `users`, `businesses`, `memberships` (owner), `sessions` rows; `planExpiresAt` = now + 30 days; full chart (`accounts`) and tax model seeded in the same transaction.
- **Expected accounting:** nothing posts.
- **Expected dashboard:** `/app` empty state that says so; `/app/billing` shows trial with days left.
- **Expected audit:** none today. `createBusinessWithOwner` writes no `audit_events` row; journey C1 expects `business.created` naming the user, tracked as gap G-50. The pass condition below does not depend on it.
- **Pass:** all of the above; a second `POST /v1/businesses` with the same grant creates nothing new; a forged setup cookie is refused.

### J2 · First WhatsApp text transaction

- **Preconditions:** J1; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set; business has no products.
- **Test data:** message "sold 3 bags of rice to Ada 08031234567 for 45k, she paid cash".
- **Action:** send from the merchant's number to Rekoda's number.
- **Status:** PASS: real-handset acceptance on staging (26 Sep 2026, reported by the owner); G-48 STAGING ACCEPTED and CLOSED. An initially paid sale ends in its receipt (spec §15, journey C5); before G-48 it produced the `INV-…` invoice PDF stamped "Paid in full" and no receipt.
- **Expected WhatsApp:** a CG2 preview naming the customer token rehydrated as "Ada", 3 × bag of rice, ₦45,000, paid ₦45,000, balance ₦0; then after "yes", the "issued" reply naming the receipt ("Receipt RCT-… is on its way.") and the receipt PDF with the merchant-recorded caption, never "confirmed".
- **Expected API/DB:** `external_events` one row for the wamid; `conversation_messages` inbound stored tokenised; `command_drafts` pending then confirmed; `customers` and `customer_identities` (vaulted); `invoices` one `INV-…` row with status `paid`; `payments` with `initialConfirmationSource = MERCHANT_ATTESTED`, `method = cash` and its allocation; one `receipts` row for that payment, `snapshot.verified = false`; `usage_counters` one `AI_ACTIONS` unit consumed; `usage_events` one `llm_call` row with tokens and cost.
- **Expected accounting:** DR Cash 45,000 / CR Sales Revenue 45,000 (plus COGS only if the product had a cost).
- **Expected dashboard:** `/app` money in (recorded, not verified) ₦45,000; `/app/invoices` one paid row; `/app/receipts` one row, recorded not verified.
- **Expected audit:** `invoice` / `issued` naming the actor and the draft; `sale.recorded` is the outbox event, not an audit row.
- **Pass:** figures in the reply equal the rows; the log contains no phone number, name or body; a replayed webhook produces no second row and no second reply.

### J3 · Sale, invoice, Paystack payment, receipt, ledger

- **Preconditions:** J1; Paystack TEST key connected via `/app/payments`; R2 configured.
- **Test data:** "sold 2 generators to Chidi chidi@example.com for 350k, not paid" then "payment details".
- **Action:** confirm the sale; ask for payment details; pay the intent with a Paystack test card or transfer.
- **Expected WhatsApp:** invoice PDF `INV-2026-…` with balance ₦350,000; the payment link; after the webhook, a receipt PDF (delivered only if the merchant wrote within the last 24 hours, G-67) with the `paymentConfirmed` caption "Money in ✅ ₦350,000 confirmed for INV-…. Receipt RCT-… is attached. Forward it to your customer." (PROVIDER VERIFIED wording; the builder joins its two sentences with a line break).
- **Expected API/DB:** `payment_intents` succeeded; `external_events` one Paystack `charge.success`; `payments` `PROVIDER_VERIFIED`; allocation to the invoice; `invoices` status `paid`; receipt row with `snapshot.verified = true`; document object in R2 under a business-scoped key.
- **Expected accounting:** at issue DR Accounts Receivable 350,000 / CR Sales Revenue 350,000; at payment DR Payment Provider Clearing 350,000 / CR Accounts Receivable 350,000 (`settle.ts` books to `PAYMENT_PROVIDER_CLEARING` whenever the payment connection resolves that account; the DR Bank form is only the degraded path with no clearing account); the settlement sweep then credits the clearing account, with fee components reconciling to gross.
- **Expected dashboard:** `/app/payments` shows the payment VERIFIED; `/app/invoices` paid; `/app/reports` balance sheet balanced.
- **Expected audit:** `audit_events` rows `invoice` / `issued` and `payment` / `confirmed` (entity and action are separate columns). No receipt audit row is written today (G-37 covers audit coverage).
- **Pass:** ledger debits equal credits; a replayed `charge.success` is `already_booked` with no second receipt; the invoice cannot be voided (`has_payments`).

### J4 · Expense, confirmation, books, report

- **Preconditions:** J1.
- **Test data:** "paid 35k for fuel today".
- **Expected WhatsApp:** the CG2 preview (`Expense: …` / `Category: …` / `*Amount: ₦35,000*` / `Paid by cash`); after "yes", "Saved ✅ ₦35,000 expense: fuel. It is in your books." (`expenseSaved`).
- **Expected DB:** an `expenses` row with category `power` (the classifier maps fuel, petrol and NEPA there; `fuel` is not a category), status `recorded`, `ledger_transaction_id` set.
- **Expected accounting:** DR Operating Expenses 35,000 / CR Cash 35,000.
- **Expected dashboard:** `/app/expenses` one row; `/app/reports` P&L expenses ₦35,000 in the current Lagos month.
- **Pass:** voiding from the dashboard writes the mirror posting, the entry stays marked `voided`, and P&L returns to zero.

### J5 · Purchase, inventory, supplier payable

- **Test data:** "bought 20 bags of rice from Musa for 400k, paid 250k".
- **Expected WhatsApp:** preview naming 20 bags, ₦400,000, paid ₦250,000, owed ₦150,000; then "Saved ✅ ₦400,000 stock purchase. <product> is now 20 on hand. ₦150,000 still owed to your supplier." (`purchaseSaved`, three lines joined with line breaks); the `BILL-…` number is on the `bills` row and the expenses page, not in the reply.
- **Expected DB:** `products` rice; `inventory_movements` +20 at unit cost 20,000; `bills` `BILL-…` balance due 150,000; `suppliers` row with vaulted name.
- **Expected accounting:** DR Inventory 400,000 / CR Cash 250,000 / CR Accounts Payable 150,000.
- **Expected dashboard:** `/app/stock` rice 20 on hand; `/app/expenses` payables ₦150,000.
- **Pass:** paying the supplier ₦150,000 from the dashboard clears the bill and AP; paying more is refused `more_than_owed`.

### J6 · Voice-note transaction (staging)

- **Preconditions:** `VOICE_TRANSCRIPTION_ENABLED=1`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AI_TRANSCRIPTION_PRICES`.
- **Test data:** a 12-second OGG voice note saying "I sold five cartons of milk to Ngozi for twelve thousand five hundred, she transferred".
- **Expected WhatsApp:** the same CG2 preview as text; a note whose container cannot be measured gets the `voiceUnreadable` reply ("Something about that voice note did not come through properly …") with nothing metered (`inbound-message.handler.ts:728-737`); a measurable note the transcriber turns into no text throws a billed `TranscriptionUnavailable` (`stt.openai.ts:60`), so the `VOICE_MINUTES` unit is refunded but the daily voice-seconds reservation stays and the reply is `voiceUnavailable` ("I could not listen to that voice note just now …"), which reads as an outage (G-66).
- **Expected DB:** `usage_events` one `transcription` row with `localSeconds` 12 and `providerSeconds` within tolerance; `voice_second_counters` +12; audio not persisted anywhere.
- **Pass:** figures match; a 130-second note is refused before any provider call; the daily ceiling refuses at the limit.

### J7 · Receipt photo transaction (staging)

- **Preconditions:** `IMAGE_AI_ENABLED=1`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- **Test data:** a phone photo of a thermal-printer receipt for ₦8,450 with a caption "fuel".
- **Expected WhatsApp:** preview "Fuel ₦8,450"; a photo of a cat gets the `notABusinessDocument` reply ("… does not look like a receipt, invoice or statement I can record from") after the vision call has already run, so the monthly `DOCUMENTS_UNDERSTOOD` unit and the daily extraction slot stay consumed and only the `AI_ACTIONS` unit is spared (`inbound-message.handler.ts:237,336-346,557-560`; nothing refunds a junk read); a ₦600,000 invoice photo with a verifier configured gets a second reading and, on disagreement, the field-naming reply.
- **Expected DB:** `usage_events` `ocr_vision` row; `doc_extraction_counters` +1; image not persisted.
- **Pass:** as above; a PDF attachment is refused with zero provider requests.

### J8 · Customer owes, later payment, reconciliation

- **Test data:** J3's unpaid invoice; then "Chidi paid 350k by transfer"; then a bank CSV import containing the credit.
- **Expected WhatsApp:** "who owes me" lists Chidi ₦350,000; after the payment message, the "Saved ✅ … recorded against INV…" text reply, then the receipt PDF (delivered only if the merchant wrote within the last 24 hours, G-67) with the `receiptRecordedReady` caption ("Receipt RCT… for ₦… on INV… is attached. Forward it to your customer."); MERCHANT CONFIRMED wording throughout, never "verified".
- **Expected DB:** `payments` `MERCHANT_ATTESTED` + `BANK_TRANSFER`; after the CSV import and reconcile, a `bank_line_matches` row tier 1 or 2, `decided_by = auto`.
- **Expected accounting:** DR Bank / CR Accounts Receivable 350,000 at attestation; nothing posts from the bank line on reconcile or match (only an explicit `POST /v1/bank/classify` posts, and this journey does not use it).
- **Pass:** a `bank_line_matches` row, tier 1 or 2 with `decided_by = 'auto'`, against the payment's ledger transaction; the `payments` row untouched; no second payment. Raising the payment's provenance to externally verified on a bank match is gap G-51 (`BANK_FEED_MATCH` is declared and never written), so the attestation stands unchanged.

### J9 · Partial payment

- **Test data:** an unpaid ₦100,000 invoice; "Ada paid 40k cash".
- **Expected:** allocation 40,000 against that invoice; status `partially_paid` (stored, recomputed on each settle); balance ₦60,000 in the reply and the register; DR Cash 40,000 / CR AR 40,000.
- **Pass (G-49, OWN-16; staging accepted):** a second "paid 70k" is answered with a CG2 preview naming the amount received (₦70,000), the amount applied (₦60,000) and the ₦10,000 as customer credit (or as unapplied, not linked to a customer, when the invoice names none); nothing posts until "yes". After "yes": one payment of ₦70,000, one allocation of ₦60,000, the invoice paid, DR Cash 70,000 / CR AR 60,000 / CR Customer credits 10,000, a `customer_credits` row of ₦10,000 keyed on the payment (named customer only), an `overpaid` reconciliation row, and a receipt for ₦70,000 naming the credit. If another payment lands between the preview and the "yes", nothing is written and the merchant is asked again.

### J10 · Overpayment

- **Test data:** ₦60,000 balance; provider webhook for ₦75,000.
- **Expected:** allocation 60,000; `customer_credits` grant 15,000 keyed on the payment; CR Customer Credit 15,000; the receipt caption names the full ₦75,000 confirmed (no reply names the excess on the provider path; the "paid over" sentence exists only in the chat sale preview); the reconciliation row reads `overpaid`.
- **Pass:** the credit is granted and no invoice is reduced by it. Applying the credit to a later invoice, and showing it on the customer statement, have no merchant-reachable path today (gap G-52: `applyCreditToInvoice` has no route and the statement has no unapplied-credit leg).

### J11 · Reversal, refund, credit

- **Test data:** a paid invoice; issue a credit note of ₦20,000 from the dashboard; then inject a Paystack `refund.processed` for the original charge.
- **Expected:** credit note creates `CUSTOMER_CREDIT` liability with proportional VAT; the refund writes a `refunds` row and a reversing posting and the invoice returns to unpaid.
- **Status:** both halves pass against fixtures (`adjustments.integration.test.ts`, 11 Sep 2026); the real Paystack envelope is still to be confirmed under G-05 (code complete, not live-verified).

### J12 · Stock purchase, sale, stock reduction

- **Test data:** J5's 20 bags; storefront order for 3 bags at the catalogue price; then "stock".
- **Expected:** server-priced order; on confirmation `inventory_movements` −3 reason `sale` in the same transaction as the invoice; COGS 60,000 posted at weighted average; "stock" answers 17 bags with no model call.
- **Pass:** two simultaneous orders for the last unit: exactly one succeeds; the loser sees the out-of-stock message and the API log shows no 500. BLOCKED by G-53 until it closes: today the loser gets the generic "did not go through" message from an uncaught `InsufficientStock`.

### J13 · Monthly statements, PDF and Excel

- **Test data:** the month of J2–J12.
- **Expected:** `GET /v1/reports/statements.pdf?period=YYYY-MM` is a real A4 PDF with the four statements; `.xlsx` opens in Excel with one sheet per statement and numeric cells; both agree with `/app/reports`; the balance sheet reports `balanced: true`; exports consume `REPORT_EXPORTS` and the 429 message appears at the cap.
- **Pass:** trial balance nets to zero; assets = liabilities + equity + profit.

### J14 · Accountant access

- **Test data:** owner invites an accountant by phone; accountant signs in.
- **Expected:** accountant reads every report and ledger view except the five owner-only reads (`GET /v1/reports/portability.json`, `GET /v1/businesses/settings`, `GET /v1/businesses/members`, `GET /v1/api-keys` and `GET /v1/webhooks` answer 403), downloads the audit CSV and reconciles bank lines; every HTTP write door (void, settings, team, billing) answers 403 and the two chat doors (sale, expense) answer the view-only reply; the delegate can record trade but not reconcile or void; removing the owner is refused with 400 (`CannotRemoveOwner`).
- **Pass:** the live matrix in `roles.integration.test.ts` reproduced through the browser.

### J15 · Trial to paid plan (staging)

- **Test data:** a business on day 20 of trial; `POST /v1/billing/quote` then `/plan` for Chat; pay the Paystack charge.
- **Expected:** the plan changes only after the provider confirms (never on the merchant's say-so); `subscription_charges` settled; `billing.process` never touches the merchant's ledger; allowances reset to the plan's table.
- **Pass:** a partial payment does not unlock; an overpayment unlocks and the excess is an operator decision.

### J16 · Failed subscription, grace, read-only

- **Test data:** a paid business whose cycle ends today; run the renewal sweep, then the grace sweep at days 1, 5 and 7.
- **Expected:** a renewal charge opens; reminders on days 1 and 5 via `META_BILLING_TEMPLATE`; day 7 read-only (`GRACE_DAYS = 7`) with books intact and exportable; the billing page copy per OD-5.
- **Pass:** a sale attempt on day 8 is refused with the `trialEnded` reply ("Your 30-day free trial has ended … Reply `*upgrade*` …"; the copy calls a lapsed paid plan a trial, noted under G-16); `GET /v1/reports/portability.json` still works (a second call inside `PORTABILITY_GAP_SECONDS` is throttled with 429).

### J17 · STOP then START

- **Test data:** "STOP", then a receipt is due, then "START", then "resend".
- **Status:** the padded-`start` clause below is the canonical outcome; G-24 is code complete (1 Oct 2026, in review) and awaits this journey on staging; the pass condition does not depend on it.
- **Expected:** after STOP no proactive send reaches the merchant (the document is rendered and stored, delivery suppressed); "resend" is honoured because the merchant asked; after START delivery resumes; a padded "start" inside 400 dashes is not treated as START (G-24).
- **Pass:** `users.opted_out_at` set on STOP and cleared on START. A repeat STOP overwrites the timestamp (`setOptOut` is an unconditional update); the first-refusal preservation exists only on `customer_message_optouts`.

### J18 · Data deletion and retention

- **Test data:** "delete my data" twice within the window; a business abandoned 90 days ago with `META_RETENTION_TEMPLATE` set.
- **Expected:** the two-ask erasure removes every `customer_identities` row and emits `data.erased` carrying only the count and source type; the retention sweep warns, then deletes the due business through the `SECURITY DEFINER` function, queues its R2 objects for deletion (the drain performs them), and leaves `retention_deletions`; with the template unset the sweep deletes nothing.
- **Pass:** no PII remains in any table or object. `customer_message_optouts` survive the two-ask erasure; the retention deletion removes them with every other `business_id` table (gap G-55 records the undecided consent semantics).

### J19 · Duplicate delivery, provider retry, idempotency

- **Test data:** the same Meta wamid delivered eight times concurrently; the same Paystack `charge.success` three times; a `POST /api/v1/sales` replayed with the same idempotency key.
- **Expected:** one `external_events` row and one job each; one booking; the API replay returns the first response.
- **Pass:** counts from SQL equal one.

### J20 · Cross-tenant attack attempt

- **Test data:** two businesses A and B; A's session; B's invoice id, customer id, product id, shop slug, export kind.
- **Expected:** every A request naming B's ids answers 404 or empty, never B's data; `?businessId=B` on any route is inert; a status webhook for B's number never lands under A (today a status whose recipient is also a merchant is filed under that merchant, G-20; this clause passes once G-20 closes); the app role cannot read `payment_intents` across tenants.
- **Pass:** the cross-tenant cases of `roles.integration.test.ts` reproduced through HTTP on staging; `rls-invariants.integration.test.ts` (a catalogue suite over `pg_policy` and `pg_class`, no HTTP) run once against the staging database with the owner credential.

### 11.2 Bring-up order

1. Close G-08's owner half (the template was corrected on 12 Sep 2026 and is guarded in CI): fill the staging `.env` from §11.1, generate the five security keys for staging, decide OD-4 flags.
2. Provision the staging host exactly as `docs/runbooks/deploy.md` "First deployment on a clean host" says (G-01 is code complete): a machine with Docker, Cloudflare DNS for the staging site and API hostnames, `secrets/postgres_owner_password`, the filled `.env`, then `dc build`. `REKODA_TRUSTED_PROXIES` and `REKODA_TRUSTED_WEB` are set by the compose file.
3. Database: `dc up -d --wait postgres`, then `dc run --rm -T migrate` (every migration as the owner, then the `rekoda_app` and `rekoda_worker` passwords from `.env`); `dc up -d --wait`; confirm `GET /health` reports 152 migrations and the release.
4. Storage: create the staging R2 bucket; boot the API with the R2 keys; write and read one document (G-40).
5. Web: set the legal values (staging placeholders only while the staging hostname is not shared or linked anywhere, since the host itself answers publicly for certificates; changing them later is a new release, the whole `deploy.md` "Deploy a release" sequence); confirm `next start` boots. Leave `META_ACCESS_TOKEN` unset until step 6: in production mode the API refuses to boot with a token and no `META_OTP_TEMPLATE` value (it cannot know whether the template is approved).
6. Meta: register the webhook URL, complete the handshake, submit the three templates on the test WABA; set `META_ACCESS_TOKEN`; run J1 (dev OTP reveal disabled, a real test handset), J17 and J19.
7. AI: set the Anthropic key; run J2, J4 and J5 live; run the eval (G-07) and record the numbers.
8. Media: enable voice and image with test budgets; run J6 and J7.
9. Paystack: connect a TEST key from `/app/payments`; run J3, J8, J9, J10, J11 (its live half is the G-05 drill; G-06 is code complete), J15, J16.
10. Operations: enable backups (G-02) and run one restore into a fresh database; wire the alert set (G-26); force each alert once.
11. Run J12, J13, J14, J18, J20; then GATE 12 in full and record the results in §9.

## 13. Security review summary (10 Sep 2026)

Application-layer security is strong: tenancy by `withBusiness()` and six RLS invariants, boot refusal of bypass roles, `SECURITY DEFINER` functions with pinned `search_path`, webhooks verified over raw bytes with length-checked constant-time compares, 128 KB pre-parse caps, DNS-rebinding-proof outbound SSRF guard, integer kobo everywhere with server-side recomputation, structural prompt-injection containment (one zod tool, ₦10bn ceiling, preview and confirm), tokenisation before every model call, AES-256-GCM vault with AAD binding and downgrade refusal, disclosed media processing, byte-sniffed uploads, OIDC operator plane failing closed, no committed credentials, full-history secret scan. The launch risk is operational, not in the code. Findings and their gap IDs: no backups (G-02), no deployment topology (G-01), `CONNECTION_KEY` not enrolled (G-13), per-process rate limiter (G-43), sessions without an absolute cap (G-25), `/health` oracle (G-46), no dependency-audit gate (G-42), the `.env.example` drift (G-08, template half closed 12 Sep 2026). CSP `unsafe-inline` for scripts is a documented Next.js trade-off; the API sets no helmet headers (low, JSON API behind CORS allowlist; add `nosniff` and HSTS with G-01).

## 14. Go / no-go and rollback

**Go to private beta** when: every P0 in §4 that is a code gap is CLOSED (G-01, G-02, G-07, G-08; G-06 is code complete and closes only under G-05); G-03, G-04 and G-05 may be carried into private beta on a test WABA, staging legal placeholders and test-mode Paystack keys, and must close for public launch; GATES 1–11 show no FAIL on a P0 or P1 row other than the carried G-03, G-04 and G-05 rows and a P1 row whose deferral an owner ruling in §6 records (P2 rows may read FAIL and are marked deferred); every P1 gap in §8, whether or not a gate row names it, is CLOSED or carries a deferral recorded in §6; journeys J1–J13, J17, J19, J20 PASS on staging with test-mode providers; a restore drill from an off-box backup has been executed within the last 7 days; the alert set has fired once each; the owner has signed the AI eval numbers. G-48 has no deferral path: J2 must PASS and cannot until G-48 is CLOSED, so a deferral ruling on G-48 would leave this bar unreachable.

**Go to public launch** when, additionally: §47 confirmation is on file and the live-money drill passed; Meta App Review is approved with the three templates; legal review of the compliance pack and the governing-law clause is recorded; tax and accounting sign-off is recorded; J14–J16 and J18 PASS on production configuration.

**Rollback criteria** (any one triggers a stop of new sign-ups and a decision within the hour): a ledger that does not balance for any business; a payment booked twice; a cross-tenant read or write; PII in a log line; webhook rejection rate above 5% for ten minutes; OTP send failure ratio above 20% for ten minutes; backup age above 24 hours; daily AI spend above the platform ceiling. Rollback procedure: `deploy.md` "Roll back" restores the previous image by changing `REKODA_RELEASE` (proved in CI; G-01) and, if a migration must be reversed, restores the last backup into a fresh database and replays from the outbox.
